scalars.scalar_value: Supervisory experience in a healthcare facility with working knowledge of human resources management practices and policies.
Previous experience in a leadership/supervising position within a hospitality department.

items.item_text: Valid California Driver’s License
Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Previous experience in a leadership/supervising position within a hospitality department.
Supervisory experience in a healthcare facility with working knowledge of human resources management practices and policies.

The incumbent, under the general direction of the EVS Manager, will direct, administer and coordinate the daily operations in order to provide a clean, safe and aesthetically pleasing environment for patients, visitors and staff. Provides direct supervision typically to professionals or skilled technical employees. Functions as advisor to unit and administration. Analyzes and resolves problems, interprets policies (e.g., fiscal management, HR, contracts and grants, resource management in defined areas) and demonstrates solid subject matter knowledge. Exercises judgment within defined procedures and policies to determine appropriate action. Supervises staff to assure accountability and stewardship of department resources (operational, financial, and human) in compliance with departmental goals and objectives.
Understand hospital and clinical cleaning requirements per Nursing unit
Develop and implement many internal supporting programs
Knowledge of health care custodial cleaning standards.
Intermediate computer application skills. Ability to collect, compile, compute and analyze statistical data, etc.
Ability to establish and maintain work standards adhering to health and safety requirements.
Knowledge and understanding of staffing schedules to cover a seven-day work period
Knowledge of relevant regulatory and industry codes, policies, standards and requirements.
Knowledge and operation of Environmental Services trade skill equipment
Demonstrated ability to coach/instruct staff and delegate authority or seek assistance when limits of delegated authority has been reached.
Knowledge of floor surfaces and professional upkeep
Ability to deliver staff training and develop staff competencies.
Knowledge of cleaning chemicals and usage requirements
Ability to communicate clearly both verbally and in writing. Ability to articulate complex ideas to a diverse staff population.
Knowledge of solid waste management
Ability to set priorities and manage conflicting demands. Ability to work effectively under pressure meeting established goals and objectives.
Knowledge of hospital bed making techniques
Interpersonal skills to establish and maintain a friendly, welcoming environment for customers, to demonstrate an interested, understanding, compassionate and caring manner.
Knowledge of floor finishing and hospital cleaning procedures
Ability to maintain a courteous and calm demeanor when working with diverse patient and staff populations/groups.
Knowledge of recycling program and pest management

Ability to maintain composure, efficiency and a positive, customer service oriented manner during periods of peak workload, with frequent interruptions, under tight deadlines and when interacting with challenging customers who may be ill, angry or emotionally distressed.
Knowledge of clerical, storekeeping and supervisory roles/functions

Problem solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem, identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create and implement viable solutions and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties.
Knowledge of local, state and federal ordinances/ regulations
Ability to exercise discretion to ensure that patient confidentiality is maintained and a professional, respectful clinic environment exists at all times.
Knowledge of personnel services and classification procedures, also adequate staffing
Knowledge of Workers’ Compensation program and State Code Title 22 on hazardous waste
